name: WV-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+20 partisan lean makes WV-02 one of the most Republican House districts in the country
Incumbent Riley Moore holds a roughly 6-to-1 fundraising advantage over challenger Ace Parsi
Prediction markets price Democratic chances at about 3%
No public polls or expert ratings track the race; nothing indicates competitiveness
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: the district's R+20 lean, Moore's incumbency and dominant fundraising edge, and market pricing that leaves Democrats with only about a 3% chance. With no polling or expert ratings suggesting competitiveness, the seat is a safe Republican hold.
model.watch: Only an extraordinary national midterm wave or a late surge of outside spending behind Parsi would put this seat on the board.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
WV-02 spans central West Virginia and carries a partisan lean of roughly R+20, placing it among the most Republican House districts in the country. First-term Representative Riley Moore is running for reelection, while Democrat Ace Parsi, a challenger without prior office, has raised about $250,000 to Moore's $1.6 million and holds far less cash on hand.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings track the race, so the picture rests on district fundamentals and market pricing. Prediction markets give Democrats roughly a 3 percent chance of an upset. Fundraising, incumbency, and the district's partisan makeup all point in the same direction, making the realistic question the size of Moore's winning margin rather than which party carries the seat.
